items.title: Supreme Court orders constitution of panels of lawyers, sign language interpreters to assist disabled advocates
items.summary: The Supreme Court will set up a permanent committee to address issues concerning the rights of disabled persons, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant announced on Wednesday. CJI Kant also directed the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to constitute panels of young lawyers and sign language interpreters to assist advocates with disabilities during proceedings before the Court. The announcements were made during a meeting between CJI Kant and Heba Hagrass , the United Nations' Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities at the Supreme Court. Lawyers with disabilities and representatives of civil society also attended the meeting. During the interaction, CJI Kant observed that ensuring the rights of disabled persons is a constitutional obligation and that equality is a fundamental principle of the Constitution. He stressed the need to identify gaps in the implementation of laws and government schemes to ensure that persons with disabilities could exercise their rights in practice. items.title: Transman should be referred to as 'male' in official records: Madras High Court to Nurses and Midwives body
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently ordered the Tamil Nadu Nurses and Midwives Council to record a member's gender identity simply as "male" and drop any references to his being "transgender male" in public or official records concerning him. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy held that the authorities cannot insist on referring to the member as a "transgender" male in official communications once his gender change has been legally certified. "It should be pure and simple male," the Court directed in its August 18 order. The Court explained that under Section 7 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, once a person has undergone the gender affirmation surgery and the District Magistrate has issued a gender affirmation certificate, the gender change must be given effect to by all authorities. Relying on the Supreme Court's landmark right to privacy ruling in Justice KS Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India , the Court further observed that the right to construct one's own gender identity falls squarely within the fundamental right to privacy. items.title: Supreme Court orders search for World War II veteran's heirs after Centre alleges possible fraud in pension claim
items.summary: The Central government on Wednesday informed the Supreme Court that an application seeking pension benefits on behalf of a war veteran was filed before the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) more than a year after his death. A special Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice SVN Bhatti said the authorities should have exercised due diligence when the case was filed in the soldier's name. It added that an inquiry was necessary to investigate the alleged fraud. "If fraud has been played on court, then we have to detect it," CJI Kant said. The Court directed the Army authorities to ascertain the identity of Rawat's legal heirs and family members. It also ordered the jurisdictional Senior Superintendent of Police and police station to provide full assistance in the exercise. The case concerns Govind Singh Rawat, a former rifleman of the British Indian Army who sustained injuries while serving in Italy during World War II. items.title: Madras High Court refuses to lift construction freeze around Pallikaranai marshland
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Wednesday declined to lift restrictions on construction within a one-kilometre radius of Chennai's Pallikaranai Marshland Ramsar Site [CREDAI Vs Member Secretary] A Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan was dealing with petitions filed by the Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India (CREDAI), resident welfare associations and others challenging the restrictions imposed pursuant to orders passed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT). Considering that a related matter is pending before the Supreme Court, the High Court observed that judicial discipline requires it to refrain from passing any orders. "Judicial discipline demands that when the highest court of the land is actively monitoring the ground-truthing and boundary demarcation of the very same wetland, a High Court must refrain from passing parallel or conflicting orders altering its protective perimeter ," the Bench said. items.title: Dispute over posthumous release of Siddhu Moose Wala's Phantom Ferrari song: Delhi HC refers case to mediation
items.summary: A dispute over whether music label Saga Music holds the rights to release the video of the "Phantom Ferrari" song sung by late singer Siddhu Moose Wala posthumously has been referred to mediation by the Delhi High Court. Siddhu Moose Wala’s parents have opposed the song's release, arguing that their permission has not been taken for releasing the song. On the other hand, Saga Music has asserted that the song's copyright was assigned to it by Moose Wala before his demise. Justice Manoj Jain today urged the parties to try and settle the dispute amicable manner. "Your son enjoys popularity sitting in heaven… It is better advised for both parties to find an amicable solution," the judge said, addressing the parents' counsel. The counsel said that he had no objection if the matter is referred to mediation. He also assured the Court that the parents will not issue any further statements to aggravate the dispute for the timebeing. items.title: Supreme Court dismisses review petition in Ujjain Takiya Masjid demolition case

items.title: Taj Trapezium Zone: Supreme Court orders fresh meeting of CEC and TTZ body after internal discord over manufacturing cluster
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and the Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) Authority to hold a fresh meeting regarding the proposed Integrated Manufacturing Cluster in Agra near the Taj Mahal. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the direction after being informed of an internal disagreement over the clearance earlier granted to the proposed industrial project within the 10,400 sq. km eco-sensitive zone. "It seems to us that there is a necessity to hold a fresh meeting between the TTZ authority and the CEC to iron out the glitches and submit a joint comprehensive report. Let the meeting be held, the conditions discussed, and a joint report be submitted within two weeks," the Court ordered. items.title: Ship can't be arrested to recover wages of another vessel's crew under same management: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday held that a ship cannot be arrested to recover crew wages relating to another vessel merely because they are managed by the same shipping company [ Light House Marine Service India Pvt Ltd v Charter and Parties interested in the Vessel MT Ocean Faye & ors ]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM observed that a vessel could be arrested in such circumstances only if, prima facie, there was a commonality of interest between the shipowners, along with a clear intention to defraud a creditor. Merely because the vessels were managed by the same entity did not mean that the entity also owned them, the Court pointed out. The Court made the observation while dismissing an appeal filed by a manning agent (crew-supply agent) named Light House Marine Service India Pvt Lt. Light House Marine Service (appellant) had sought to arrest the vessel MT Ocean Faye to recover wages it had paid to crew members of three other vessels, all of which are managed by Star Voyages Shipping Services LLC.
